Rishi / Neha —

I ran the quick sanity pass and attached the preliminary results (prelim_eval_results-redwood-20260216.tar.gz). Below is a short summary of the 5-sample check for the two prompts across the three model variants:

Summary (5-sample per-model):
- Redwood-rlhf-v2: 0/25 hallucination flags, concise extraction, slightly more conservative on policy language (preferred for compliance). Avg latency: 180ms.
- CloudGen Text-XL: 2/25 hallucination flags (tended to speculate when context was sparse), slightly longer outputs. Avg latency: 260ms.
- AtlasText v3: 1/25 hallucination flags, faster for summaries but inconsistent extraction formatting. Avg latency: 310ms (exceeded Felicity's 300ms target in our sample).

Notes / next steps:
- Redwood shows strong early quality on the compliance prompts — low hallucination and stable formatting which helps downstream parsers.
- Recommend running full Round 1 (500 prompt pairs) with logging enabled for hallucination heuristics + automatic example sampling for manual review. This will take ~48 hours on dedicated eval fleet.
- I included a small script in the tarball (run_eval.sh) and a CSV of sampled outputs with our binary hallucination labels.

I can prepare an anonymized package with 10 failure cases and suggested prompt-tuning patches for Felicity’s trust team. If they want, we can also run a toxicity/bias pass, but that would add ~12 hours.

Let me know if you want me to upload the anonymized sample outputs to the shared doc or just attach as a ZIP in the HubSpot deal record.
